mainTopic: What the יום הכיפורים, ראש חודש and רגלים goats atone for, according to רבי ישמעאל and רבי יהודה
overview: The גמרא first finishes a point from the previous page: this atonement happens 'only once a year.' It then asks about רבי ישמעאל. In his view, someone who found out about his טומאה only at the end brings his own קרבן, so what does the outer שעיר of יום הכיפורים atone for? The answer is a case where the person never knew at all. The גמרא explains that רבי ישמעאל agrees with רבי מאיר that all the goats share one atonement. For him, the הקש of the outer goat to the inner goat teaches that neither one atones for other sins. Next the גמרא turns to רבי יהודה in the משנה, who says the ראש חודש and רגלים goats atone for טומאה no one ever knew about. שמואל finds the source in the word ״לַה׳״, meaning a sin known only to ה׳. The גמרא shows that this word also leaves room for ריש לקיש's lesson about the moon. A teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל limits the ראש חודש goat to טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. The גמרא then searches for a source for the רגלים goats, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing the earlier point: only once a year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a teaching from the previous page with the words 'only once a year.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a thought that started on the previous page. It ends with the idea that this atonement happens only once a year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line closes the earlier discussion based on the words 'אחת בשנה' in the פסוק. After it, the גמרא moves to a new question about רבי ישמעאל.

keyTerms.meaning: Once a year, words from the פסוק about the יום הכיפורים service

phrases.english: Rather, only once a year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion carried over from the previous daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The atonement under discussion takes place only once a year.

steps.title: Under רבי ישמעאל, what is left for the outer goat?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל holds that awareness only at the end obligates a קרבן. So what does the outer goat of יום הכיפורים atone for?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי ישמעאל, a person who did not know at the beginning but did know at the end must bring a קרבן. If so, what does the goat brought outside atone for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem. The case that the משנה gave to the outer goat is already covered by a personal קרבן in רבי ישמעאל's view, so what job is left for that goat?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the outer goat atones when there was no awareness at the beginning but there was awareness at the end. רבי ישמעאל says that exact person brings his own קרבן עולה ויורד. That seems to leave the outer goat with nothing to do.

keyTerms.meaning: Knowing about the טומאה before the sin
Finding out about the טומאה after the sin
Obligated to bring a קרבן
The outer goat of יום הכיפורים, whose blood is put on the outer מזבח

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yishmael, who says:
where there was no awareness at the beginning
but there was awareness at the end,
he is liable to bring an offering,
the goat whose service is done outside, what does it atone for?
phrases.notes: This is the goat whose blood goes on the outer מזבח, not inside the היכל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new line of questioning about רבי ישמעאל's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case of טומאה the outer goat atones for in רבי ישמעאל's view.

steps.title: Answer: when the person never knew at all
steps.stepSummary: The outer goat atones when there was no awareness at the beginning or at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: It atones for a case where the person never knew, neither at the beginning nor at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that in רבי ישמעאל's view, the outer goat covers someone who never found out about his טומאה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since awareness at the end now leads to a personal קרבן, the goat is given the only case left: no awareness at any point.

keyTerms.meaning: Neither at the beginning nor at the end

phrases.english: For a case where there is no awareness,
neither at the beginning nor at the end.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ יְדִיעָה לֹא בַּתְּחִלָּה וְלֹא בַּסּוֹף
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The outer goat atones for טומאה where there was never any awareness.

steps.title: But the רגלים and ראש חודש goats cover that case
steps.stepSummary: The goats of the holidays and of ראש חודש already atone when there was no awareness at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for that case, the goats of the holidays and of ראש חודש atone!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to the answer it just gave. The case of 'never knew' already belongs to other goats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה assigns 'no awareness at all' to the goats of the רגלים and ראש חודש. If the outer goat of יום הכיפורים does the same thing, it would just repeat their job.

keyTerms.meaning: The goats brought as חטאות on the holidays
The goats brought as חטאות on ראש חודש

phrases.english: But for that, the goats of the Festivals
phrases.notes: Read this as 'that case', meaning the person who never knew at all.

phrases.english: and the goats of the New Moons atone!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי שְׂעִירֵי הָרְגָלִים וּשְׂעִירֵי רָאשֵׁי חֳדָשִׁים מְכַפְּרִין
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the outer goat atones for a case with no awareness at all.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That case is already given to the רגלים and ראש חודש goats, so the outer goat would have no role of its own.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל follows רבי מאיר: all goats atone alike
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל agrees with רבי מאיר that all the goats atone for the same thing, טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי מאיר, who says that all the goats atone for the same thing: for the defiling of the מקדש and its holy foods.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection. In רבי מאיר's view, the goats are not divided into separate jobs, and רבי ישמעאל agrees with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection assumed that each goat has its own case. רבי מאיר holds that all these goats share the same atonement. So it is no problem that the outer goat and the רגלים goats cover the same case.

keyTerms.meaning: Their atonement is the same
Entering the מקדש or eating קדשים while טמא

phrases.english: He holds like Rabbi Meir, who says:
the atonement of all the goats is the same:
for the defiling of the Temple and its sacred foods.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the view to a different תנא's framework
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each goat must have its own separate case of atonement.
steps.terutzMaskana: In רבי מאיר's view, which רבי ישמעאל accepts, all the goats share one atonement, so overlap is fine.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבי ישמעאל's view fits with רבי מאיר's approach, not with the views in the משנה that give each group of goats its own separate case.

steps.title: Then why does the תורה link the outer goat to the inner one?
steps.stepSummary: If the outer goat does not share the inner goat's special job, what does the הקש between them teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, for what law is the outer goat linked to the inner goat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question about the הקש. It is setting up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה links the outer goat to the inner goat. Earlier this link taught that the outer goat, like the inner one, atones only where there was some awareness. Under רבי ישמעאל the outer goat now covers a case with no awareness at all, so the link needs a new purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: For what law, meaning what does it teach?
Was linked through a הקש
The outer goat and the inner goat of יום הכיפורים

phrases.english: But for what law
is the outer goat linked to the inner goat?
phrases.notes: The inner goat's blood is brought inside the היכל; the outer goat's goes on the outer מזבח.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאי הִלְכְתָא אִיתַּקַּשׁ חִיצוֹן לִפְנִימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from steps 2 to 5: the outer goat now has a different job, so what does the link teach?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What law the הקש of the outer goat to the inner goat teaches in רבי ישמעאל's view.

steps.title: Neither goat atones for other sins
steps.stepSummary: The inner goat does not atone for other sins, and the הקש teaches that the outer goat does not either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as the inner goat does not atone for other sins, so too the outer goat does not atone for other sins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the purpose of the הקש. Both goats are limited to טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The link no longer teaches which case of awareness each goat covers. It teaches a limit: the outer goat, like the inner goat, atones only for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו and not for other sins.

keyTerms.meaning: Other sins, outside of טומאת מקדש וקדשיו

steps.whatToRemember: In רבי ישמעאל's view, the outer goat atones for טומאה with no awareness at all, following רבי מאיר that all goats atone alike. The הקש to the inner goat teaches that it does not atone for other sins.

phrases.english: Just as the inner one does not atone
for other transgressions,
so too the outer one does not atone
for other transgressions.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה פְּנִימִי אֵינוֹ מְכַפֵּר בִּשְׁאָר עֲבֵירוֹת
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The הקש teaches that the outer goat, like the inner one, atones only for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו and not for other sins.

steps.title: The משנה: holiday and ראש חודש goats atone when no one ever knew
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. According to רבי יהודה, the goats of the רגלים and of ראש חודש atone for טומאה that no one knew about at the beginning or at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a case of טומאה where there was no awareness at the beginning or at the end, the goats of the Festivals and the goats of ראש חודש bring atonement. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה so that it can explain it. This line sets up the next question: what is רבי יהודה's source?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is someone who became טמא and entered the מקדש or ate קדשים, and never knew it at any point. רבי יהודה says the goats brought as חטאות on the רגלים and on ראש חודש atone for this.

keyTerms.meaning: The goats brought as חטאות on the Festivals (פסח, שבועות, סוכות)
The goats brought as חטאות on ראש חודש
Awareness at the beginning or at the end; here neither one ever happened
They bring atonement

phrases.english: For [defilement] in which there is no awareness
phrases.notes: This means becoming טמא and then entering the מקדש or eating קדשים.

phrases.english: neither at the beginning nor at the end,
the goats of the Festivals
and the goats of the New Moons atone.
These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ יְדִיעָה בַּתְּחִלָּה וְלֹא בַּסּוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of רבי ישמעאל and the outer goat to a new line of the משנה with רבי יהודה's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the goats of the רגלים and ראש חודש atone for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו where there was never any awareness.

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, asks what source רבי יהודה has for his rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: What is the reason of רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל asks where רבי יהודה learns his rule from. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה gave a specific job to the holiday and ראש חודש goats. שמואל wants a פסוק that ties these goats to a sin that no one ever knew about.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason or source?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רב יהודה, the אמורא who quotes שמואל, with רבי יהודה, the תנא in the משנה. They are two different people from different generations.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה's ruling quoted in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches רבי יהודה's rule.

steps.title: ״לַה׳״: a sin only ה׳ knows about
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the ראש חודש goat is ״לְחַטָּאת לַה׳״, which is read as "a sin known only to ה׳." So this goat atones for a sin that no person ever knew about.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "And one goat for a sin-offering to ה׳." This means that for a sin which only ה׳ knows about, this goat will atone.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the source. The words ״לְחַטָּאת לַה׳״ are read as "a sin that belongs only to ה׳," meaning only He knows about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If neither the person nor anyone else ever found out, only ה׳ knows about the sin. That fits exactly the case of no awareness at the beginning or at the end.

keyTerms.meaning: To ה׳. Here it is read as a sin known only to ה׳
Recognizes it or knows about it

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole rest of the סוגיא argues about this one word, ״לַה׳״.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"And one goat for a sin-offering to the Lord"
phrases.notes: במדבר 28:15. This is the פסוק about the ראש חודש offerings.

phrases.aramaic: חֵטְא שֶׁאֵין מַכִּיר בּוֹ אֶלָּא ה׳,
phrases.english: a sin that no one recognizes except the Lord,
this goat shall atone for it.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word ״לַה׳״ in the פסוק about the ראש חודש goat teaches that it atones for a sin known only to ה׳.

steps.title: But ריש לקיש needs ״לַה׳״ for the moon
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that ריש לקיש already uses ״לַה׳״ for something else: ה׳ says this goat is an atonement for His making the moon smaller.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this word is needed for ריש לקיש's teaching. ריש לקיש said: Why is the ראש חודש goat different, that the פסוק says ״לַה׳״ about it? הקב״ה said: Let this goat be an atonement for My having made the moon smaller.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's source. It says the word ״לַה׳״ is already being used for a different lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word in the תורה usually teaches one thing. If ״לַה׳״ is needed to teach that the goat atones for ה׳'s making the moon smaller, it seems it cannot also be the source for רבי יהודה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it for another teaching
What is different about this?
I made the moon smaller

phrases.english: But this is needed for that which Reish Lakish taught,
as Reish Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: מָה נִשְׁתַּנָּה שָׂעִיר שֶׁל רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ
phrases.english: What is different about the goat of the New Moon
that "to the Lord" is said about it?
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
This goat shall be an atonement
for My having made the moon smaller.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source given in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's use of ״לַה׳״ as the source for רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word is already used for ריש לקיש's lesson about the moon, so it seems it is not free to teach רבי יהודה's rule.

steps.title: The wording ״לַה׳״ instead of ״עַל ה׳״ teaches both
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק meant only ריש לקיש's lesson, it would have said ״עַל ה׳״. Since it says ״לַה׳״, it also teaches שמואל's lesson: a sin known only to ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the פסוק say ״עַל ה׳״. Why does it say ״לַה׳״? To teach what we said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The exact wording of the פסוק shows that it teaches more than ריש לקיש's lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש's lesson alone, ״עַל ה׳״ ("for ה׳") would have been enough. The תורה chose ״לַה׳״, which can also be read as "a sin that belongs to ה׳ alone." So the word teaches both lessons, and רבי יהודה's source stands.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Let the פסוק say
For ה׳, on His behalf
For what we said

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה learns from ״לַה׳״ that the ראש חודש goat atones for טומאה known only to ה׳. The same word also teaches ריש לקיש's lesson about the moon, because the תורה wrote ״לַה׳״ and not ״עַל ה׳״.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say "for the Lord";
why does it say "to the Lord"?
For that which we said.
phrases.notes: Meaning the lesson from step 10: a sin that only ה׳ knows about.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise wording: the specific form ״לַה׳״ carries an extra lesson beyond ריש לקיש's teaching.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״לַה׳״ is fully used up by ריש לקיש's lesson about the moon.
steps.terutzMaskana: ריש לקיש's lesson would only need ״עַל ה׳״, so ״לַה׳״ also teaches רבי יהודה's rule.

steps.title: Maybe the whole word teaches only שמואל's lesson
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: perhaps ״לַה׳״ comes entirely to teach 'a sin known only to ה׳,' and not ריש לקיש's lesson at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that the whole phrase comes only for this lesson!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 12's answer that ״לַה׳״ teaches both lessons. It asks: maybe the whole phrase teaches only שמואל's lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said the wording ״לַה׳״ (instead of ״עַל ה׳״) shows that שמואל's lesson is included too. Now the גמרא flips it around and asks why we should not say the phrase teaches only שמואל's lesson. That would leave nothing for ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: But say (a challenge offering another way to read something)
All of it, the whole thing
It comes for this purpose

phrases.english: But say that the whole of it
phrases.notes: The 'whole of it' is the phrase ״לַה׳״ from the ראש חודש פסוק.

phrases.english: comes for this alone!
phrases.notes: 'This' means שמואל's lesson, a sin known only to ה׳.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 12's claim that the פסוק teaches both lessons.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion in step 12 that ״לַה׳״ teaches both ריש לקיש's and שמואל's lessons.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the wording points to שמואל's lesson, maybe it teaches only that lesson and leaves no room for ריש לקיש's lesson.

steps.title: The wording teaches two lessons
steps.stepSummary: If only שמואל's lesson were meant, the פסוק would say ״חַטָּאת ה׳״. Since it says ״לַה׳״, we learn both lessons.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the פסוק should say ״a sin-offering of ה׳״. Why does it say ״to ה׳״? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the exact wording ״לַה׳״ shows that both lessons are being taught at the same time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Had the פסוק wanted only שמואל's lesson, the shorter wording ״חַטָּאת ה׳״ would have been enough. The extra form ״לַה׳״ makes room for ריש לקיש's lesson as well. So the phrase carries two lessons together.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Let the פסוק say
Learn two things from it

steps.whatToRemember: ״לַה׳״ teaches two lessons: ריש לקיש's (atonement for making the moon smaller) and שמואל's (a sin known only to ה׳).

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say:
"A sin-offering of the Lord";
Why does it say "to the Lord"?
Learn two things from it.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase might teach only שמואל's lesson.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wording ״לַה׳״ (not ״חַטָּאת ה׳״) shows that both lessons are taught.

steps.title: Why not atone for other sins too?
steps.stepSummary: If the goat atones for a sin known only to ה׳, why limit it to טומאה? Let it atone for any unknown sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let it atone even for other sins!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ראש חודש goat atones only for unknown טומאה, and not for any sin that no one knew about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source in step 10 just says 'a sin known only to ה׳.' It does not mention טומאה. So the goat could seem to cover every hidden sin, but רבי יהודה limits it to טומאה of the מקדש and its holy food.

keyTerms.meaning: And let it atone
Other sins

phrases.english: But let it also atone
even for other sins!
phrases.notes: He means other sins that no one ever knew about, not only טומאה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the source is settled, the גמרא questions how far the goat's atonement reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's limiting the goat's atonement to טומאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source 'a sin known only to ה׳' is general, so it should cover all unknown sins.

steps.title: Compared to the יום הכפורים goat: fixed time
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל compares the ראש חודש goat to the יום הכפורים goat. Both come at a fixed time, so both atone only for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: since this one comes at a fixed time and that one comes at a fixed time, just as that one atones only for טומאה of the מקדש and its holy food, so too this one atones only for that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל. It compares the two goats because both are brought at a set time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יום הכפורים goat is known to atone only for טומאה of the מקדש and its holy food. Because both goats share a fixed time, the ראש חודש goat gets the same limit. This explains why it does not cover other sins.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל
Since
A fixed time
Entering the מקדש or eating holy food while טמא

steps.whatToRemember: The ראש חודש goat atones only for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, learned from the יום הכפורים goat because both come at a fixed time.

phrases.english: It was taught in the school of Rabbi Yishmael:
Since this one comes at a fixed time
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the ראש חודש goat.

phrases.english: and that one comes at a fixed time;
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the יום הכפורים goat.

phrases.english: just as that one atones

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: הוֹאִיל וְזֶה בָּא בִּזְמַן קָבוּעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 by limiting the goat's atonement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison based on a shared feature (fixed time)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ראש חודש goat might atone for all unknown sins.
steps.terutzMaskana: Like the יום הכפורים goat, it atones only for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.

steps.title: What is the source for the רגלים goats?
steps.stepSummary: We have a source for the ראש חודש goats. The גמרא asks where we learn the same rule for the goats of the רגלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for the goats of ראש חודש. From where do we know the goats of the רגלים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes that so far it has only proved the rule for ראש חודש. It now asks for a source for the רגלים goats, which רבי יהודה also included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's rule in step 8 covers both the ראש חודש goats and the רגלים goats. The פסוק ״לַה׳״ was said only about ראש חודש. So a separate source is needed for the רגלים.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source)
The goats brought on the festivals
From where do we know?

phrases.english: We have found a source for the goats of the New Moons;
from where do we know the goats of the Festivals?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן שְׂעִירֵי רָאשֵׁי חֳדָשִׁים, שְׂעִירֵי הָרְגָלִים מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the ראש חודש source, the גמרא moves on to the second half of רבי יהודה's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the רגלים goats also atone for unknown טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.

steps.title: Neither single comparison works for the רגלים
steps.stepSummary: Learning the רגלים from ראש חודש fails because ראש חודש is more frequent. Learning it from יום הכפורים fails because יום הכפורים atones for more. The גמרא then starts a new suggestion.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say this too can be learned like the school of רבי ישמעאל taught, it can be refuted: if from ראש חודש, that is more frequent; if from יום הכפורים, its atonement is greater! And if you say...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests learning the רגלים goats from the other goats, then shows that each single comparison has a weak point. The last words, ״וְכִי תֵּימָא״, set up the גמרא's next try, which continues after this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A comparison works only if the source case is not stronger in some way. ראש חודש comes more often than the רגלים, so it may be special. יום הכפורים atones for much more, so it may be special too. That is why neither one alone can teach the רגלים.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say
There is a way to refute it
Frequent, comes often
Its atonement is greater

steps.confusionAlert: The final ״וְכִי תֵּימָא״ is not a complete thought. It opens the גמרא's next suggestion, which continues in the following section.

phrases.english: And if you would say that this too

And if you would say:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָא נָמֵי כִּדְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible answer to step 17 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion to learn the רגלים goats from either the ראש חודש goat or the יום הכפורים goat alone.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Each source case has something extra: ראש חודש is more frequent, and יום הכפורים has greater atonement.
